sources.articleTitle: Nigeria targets 90% functional health centres, 40% health insurance coverage by 2031
FG upgrades 3,526 health centres, says 41 targets met

headline: Federal Government Reports Completion Of Health Sector Target Goals
seoTitle: Nigeria Upgrades Health Centres And Sets Future Targets
metaDescription: The Nigerian government reported 3,526 health center upgrades and outlined future healthcare goals to improve coverage and functionality by 2031.
aiSummaryBullets: The administration claims to have met 41 performance targets for the national health sector.
A total of 3,526 primary healthcare facilities have undergone revitalization efforts.
Future plans aim to increase health insurance to 40% and ensure 90% of centers are functional by 2031.
aiContextParagraph: The Nigerian Federal Government has announced progress in its ongoing health sector revitalization program under the leadership of President Bola Tinubu. According to official reports, the government successfully completed 41 performance indicators designated for the sector. As part of this initiative, authorities confirmed the upgrade of 3,526 primary healthcare centers nationwide. Looking toward the next decade, the government has established new strategic benchmarks to be achieved by 2031. These goals include raising the functionality of primary health facilities to 90 percent and increasing national health insurance coverage to 40 percent. Furthermore, the government intends to expand maternal and newborn health interventions across all 774 local government areas in the country. A central objective of these policy adjustments is to reduce the reliance on out-of-pocket health expenditure, aiming to bring it below the 50 percent threshold within the next five years.
whyItIsViral: The story is currently trending due to multiple reports from national media outlets detailing government achievements and long-term health sector policy targets.
